title: R3 disaster-recovery completion composition
description: Objective: make `recovery.complete` a real durable command that can clear QUIESCED only for the exact installed restore and fully reconciled external world. Deliverable: a daemon recovery-completion service that recomputes a versioned R3 recovery digest over BackupGeneration/cursor, RecoveryAnchor install, incarnation/key epoch, configured inventory coverage and dispositions, verifies a current HUMAN R3 approval with reason and recent step-up bound to that digest, then calls the existing project reducer and durable store exactly once. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: core `RecoveryCompletionWitness` and `reduceProject` exist and generic policy supports R3, but no daemon service builds the witness, no canonical recovery digest exists, and no approval is bound to restore/inventory bytes. NOT in scope: minting the restore identity, installing slots, enumerating external state, weakening the embargo, UI controls, GO_QUIESCE/GO_ACTIVATE, or tests/fault. Hard dependencies: task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a, task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683, task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587, and task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa must be DONE and consumed. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion.* plus minimal command-registry/index wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: The production service recomputes one canonical versioned digest over project, backup generation/cursor/RPO, installed anchor slot and command, current incarnation/key epoch, exact configured inventory class set, coverage proofs, item dispositions, quarantine refs, and reconciliation digest; callers cannot supply the accepted digest as authority.

Only a current HUMAN approval classified R3 and carrying a non-empty reason plus recent step-up reference, itself bound to that exact digest/incarnation/project, can authorize completion; system-policy, stale, carried-forward, mismatched, or weaker approvals refuse.

Missing/unverifiable evidence or unresolved UNKNOWN/quarantined inventory returns `UNKNOWN_TRUTH` or `RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` from its originating layer; digest mismatch returns `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_DIGEST_MISMATCH` at layer `RECOVERY_COMPLETION`; tests pin which layer refused first.

A valid request durably commits exactly one `recovery.complete` decision/event using the existing reducer, changes the selected database from QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED to READY, and releases the effect embargo only in the same committed authority sequence; replay returns the stored decision without a second transition.
Any post-approval change to anchor, generation, key epoch, coverage, inventory, disposition, quarantine, policy, reason, or step-up binding invalidates completion and leaves the project quiesced.
Focused tests use the shipped store, core reducer, policy approval, anchor, and inventory surfaces—not reimplemented helpers—and mutation-check the production digest comparison.

POSITIVE CONTROL: a QUIESCED project with an installed restore, a matching anchor, and a stored reconciliation record whose truth is COMPLETE and whose every item disposition is non-QUARANTINED, plus a HUMAN R3 approval whose exactRevisionHash equals the recomputed digest and which carries a non-empty decisionReason and a step-up ref inside the 300s window — assert exactly one committed recovery.complete decision, exactly one ProjectRecovered event, project state moving to READY with recoveryRequired false, and the witness carrying truthClass HUMAN_APPROVED. Then assert the embargo release the same way the embargo itself observes it: `stateOf(readDurableLedger(store, projectId), projectId)` reports READY/recoveryRequired false in that same committed sequence — the effect embargo is a pure function of that state, so asserting the state IS asserting the release, and it avoids coupling this suite to task-e33747f9's in-flight module. REFUSAL PRECEDENCE, each pinning exact code AND layer AND which layer answered FIRST: malformed envelope -> RECOVERY_COMPLETION_REQUEST_MALFORMED/DAEMON_INGRESS; unknown or unreadable reconciliation digest -> the ledger's own RECORD_NOT_FOUND / RECORD_UNREADABLE / RECORD_CONFLICT at RECOVERY_INVENTORY_LEDGER verbatim; record truth UNKNOWN or a non-null coordinator answer -> UNKNOWN_TRUTH at RECOVERY_INVENTORY verbatim; any item QUARANTINED or carrying a quarantineRef -> RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED at RECOVERY_INVENTORY (note `deriveRecoveryReconciliationTruth` treats only UNKNOWN as incomplete, so a COMPLETE record CAN carry quarantined items — this service is what refuses them, and a test must prove it); missing anchor / restore / project state or any disagreement among them -> RECOVERY_COMPLETION_EVIDENCE_ABSENT or _MISMATCH at RECOVERY_COMPLETION with upstream preserved; digest mismatch -> RECOVERY_COMPLETION_DIGEST_MISMATCH at RECOVERY_COMPLETION; SYSTEM_POLICY actor, riskTier below R3, empty or absent decisionReason, absent or stale step-up, wrong approval lifecycle -> the core `applyApprovalCommand` code surfaced verbatim, or RECOVERY_COMPLETION_APPROVAL_INVALID where core has no opinion; a non-QUIESCED project -> the core reducer's own code; CAS loss -> RECOVERY_COMPLETION_STALE with the store code in upstream. implementationPlan.description: GREEN part 1 — evidence gathering and digest comparison, in apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion.ts (+ its one-line .js bridge). The request carries POINTERS ONLY — reconciliationDigest, the approval record, the approval command, and expectedVersion — and NEVER the accepted digest itself; DoD 1 forbids a caller supplying the digest as authority, so the service recomputes it from what it reads. Snapshot every store-returned object/array through own enumerable data descriptors before use. Then call `recoveryCompletionDigest` over the assembled server-read tuple and compare it to the approval record's `exactRevisionHash`; inequality is RECOVERY_COMPLETION_DIGEST_MISMATCH at RECOVERY_COMPLETION. BYPASS TRACE. No path reaches the commit past a skipped gate. runRecoveryCompleteCommand orders decode -> durable replay -> evidence+digest -> CAS -> approval -> reduceProject -> ONE commit, and `commit()` is called from exactly one site after every gate returned ok. The digest is compared twice on independent branches (recovery-completion.ts:146 and again inside boundApproval:123), so deleting either leaves the other. The quarantine gate sits inside readRecoveryCompletionEvidence, which runs before any approval work. Every store read is individually try/caught into a typed refusal; no catch sits above a gate in a way that could swallow it into the accept path.

CALLER-SUPPLIED AUTHORITY. truthClass is a server literal at recovery-completion.ts:281; the witness hashes come from found.coverageProofHash and record.recordDigest/record.incarnationRef; the accepted digest is recomputed from server-read bytes. The envelope refuses an EXTRA payload key rather than dropping it, and the malformed sweep proves it with named "smuggled payload key" (truthClass) and "smuggled witness" cases - silently ignoring them would have looked like they were honoured.

EXOTIC INPUTS. The revoked-proxy / accessor / symbol-key / sparse class is structurally unreachable, not merely untested: readEnvelope requires `input instanceof Uint8Array` and everything downstream is the output of JSON.parse via decodeBoundedJsonBytes, which bounds size too. Array.isArray can therefore never meet a revoked proxy here. Store-returned objects are re-snapshotted through own enumerable non-getter descriptors in projectStateOf, so an accessor cannot answer twice.

WEAKER APPROVALS. A 7-case table pins R2, REJECT, an opaque step-up ref, absent and empty reason, DECIDED lifecycle and INVALIDATED validity, each with its exact code AND the layer that answered (3 at RECOVERY_COMPLETION, 4 verbatim at CORE_APPROVAL), and asserts its own length 7. A signed AGENT is refused at HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE; SYSTEM_POLICY has two separate cases, one where core answers first and one where core accepts and this layer refuses.

REPLAY. answerRecoveryCompletionReplay returns before any evidence read, re-presents the exact stored event through the store's own idempotency, and requires disposition REPLAYED plus an equal decisionSha256. Changed request bytes raise IdempotencyConflictError -> RECOVERY_COMPLETION_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The already-recovered test asserts recoveredCount stays 1.
